answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post a bid or claim a reward. If linked accounts coordinate to fake demand, validators can use signed commitments and later proof of delivery to detect mismatches, then slash the stake. Creating more identities does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital in every one and risks losing it. A fable about a haven beside a lagoon may fool readers, but it cannot satisfy the settlement rules.
